la-01-c1.text: NASA Glenn Research Center. Vectors. NASA Glenn Research Center, Beginner's Guide to Aeronautics.
la-01-c1.quote: Vector quantities have two characteristics, a magnitude and a direction.
la-01-c1.claim: That's a vector, a quantity with both magnitude (its size) and direction.

la-02-c1.text: Dan Margalit, Joseph Rabinoff. Matrix Transformations. Interactive Linear Algebra, Georgia Institute of Technology.
la-02-c1.quote: In this section we learn to understand matrices geometrically as functions, or transformations.
la-02-c1.claim: A matrix is a grid of numbers that works as a function, transforming vectors.

la-02-c3.text: J J O'Connor, E F Robertson. Matrices and determinants. MacTutor History of Mathematics, University of St Andrews.
la-02-c3.quote: Eisenstein in 1844 denoted linear substitutions by a single letter and showed how to add and multiply them like ordinary numbers except for the lack of commutativity.
la-02-c3.claim: Matrix multiplication is not commutative: AB ≠ BA in general.

la-03-c1.text: Dan Margalit, Joseph Rabinoff. Systems of Linear Equations. Interactive Linear Algebra, Georgia Institute of Technology.
la-03-c1.quote: The fact that that the lines do not intersect means that the system of equations has no solution.
la-03-c1.claim: No solution: The lines are parallel (never meet)

la-03-c2.text: J J O'Connor, E F Robertson. Matrices and determinants. MacTutor History of Mathematics, University of St Andrews.
la-03-c2.quote: Gauss gave a systematic method for solving such equations which is precisely Gaussian elimination on the coefficient matrix.
la-03-c2.claim: Gaussian elimination is a systematic method for solving systems.

la-04-c1.text: Dan Margalit, Joseph Rabinoff. Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors. Interactive Linear Algebra, Georgia Institute of Technology.
la-04-c1.quote: The German prefix “eigen” roughly translates to “self” or “own”.

la-04-c3.text: Dan Margalit, Joseph Rabinoff. Stochastic Matrices. Interactive Linear Algebra, Georgia Institute of Technology.
la-04-c3.quote: The PageRank vector is the steady state of the Google Matrix.
la-04-c3.claim: The ranking is the eigenvector of the web's link matrix

la-05-c3.text: Dan Margalit, Joseph Rabinoff. Basis and Dimension. Interactive Linear Algebra, Georgia Institute of Technology.
la-05-c3.quote: A nonzero subspace has infinitely many different bases, but they all contain the same number of vectors.
la-05-c3.claim: The dimension of a vector space is the number of vectors in any basis (they all have the same size).

la-05-c3.text: Dan Margalit, Joseph Rabinoff. The Rank Theorem. Interactive Linear Algebra, Georgia Institute of Technology.
la-05-c3.quote: In all examples, the dimension of the column space plus the dimension of the null space is equal to the number of columns of the matrix. This is the content of the rank theorem.
la-05-c3.claim: The Rank-Nullity Theorem says rank + nullity = n (the number of columns).

la-06-c2.text: Dan Margalit, Joseph Rabinoff. Dot Products and Orthogonality. Interactive Linear Algebra, Georgia Institute of Technology.
la-06-c2.quote: The closest point has the property that the difference between the two points is orthogonal, or perpendicular, to the subspace.
la-06-c2.claim: This gives the closest point on the line of a to the tip of b.

la-06-c3.text: J J O'Connor, E F Robertson. Erhard Schmidt - Biography. MacTutor History of Mathematics, University of St Andrews.
la-06-c3.quote: Schmidt is best remembered for the Gram-Schmidt orthogonalisation process, which takes a basis of a space and constructs an orthogonal one from it.
la-06-c3.claim: The Gram-Schmidt process takes any basis and produces an orthogonal one

la-07-c1.text: Dan Margalit, Joseph Rabinoff. Diagonalization. Interactive Linear Algebra, Georgia Institute of Technology.
la-07-c1.quote: Diagonal matrices are the easiest kind of matrices to understand: they just scale the coordinate directions by their diagonal entries.
la-07-c1.claim: Diagonal matrices are trivial to work with

la-07-c3.text: David Austin. We Recommend a Singular Value Decomposition. AMS Feature Column (copy hosted by the University of Toronto, Department of Mathematics).
la-07-c3.quote: Surprisingly, this seemingly modest problem turns out to be quite challenging, and the groups involved are now using rather sophisticated techniques. At the heart of all of them is the singular value decomposition.
la-07-c3.claim: In the Netflix prize, SVD factors the user-movie rating matrix to predict missing entries.

la-08-c2.text: Gilbert Strang (2011). Symmetric matrices and positive definiteness (lecture summary). MIT OpenCourseWare, 18.06SC Linear Algebra.
la-08-c2.quote: For a symmetric matrix with real number entries, the eigenvalues are real numbers and it’s possible to choose a complete set of eigenvectors that are perpendicular (or even orthonormal).

la-08-c2.text: David Austin. We Recommend a Singular Value Decomposition. AMS Feature Column (copy hosted by the University of Toronto, Department of Mathematics).
la-08-c2.quote: If we have a symmetric 2 2 matrix, it turns out that we may always rotate the grid in the domain so that the matrix acts by stretching and perhaps reflecting in the two directions. In other words, symmetric matrices behave like diagonal matrices.
la-08-c2.claim: It says every symmetric transformation is just scaling along perpendicular axes.

la-08-c3.text: Gilbert Strang (2011). Symmetric matrices and positive definiteness (lecture summary). MIT OpenCourseWare, 18.06SC Linear Algebra.
la-08-c3.quote: A positive deﬁnite matrix is a symmetric matrix A for which all eigenvalues are positive.

la-09-c2.text: He Wang. Math 5110, Section 8: Jordan Normal Form. Northeastern University, Department of Mathematics.
la-09-c2.quote: The Jordan normal form of A is unique up to the order of Jordan blocks.
la-09-c2.claim: The Jordan Normal Form Theorem states that every square matrix over the complex numbers is similar to a block-diagonal matrix of Jordan blocks

la-09-c2.text: Santiago Cañez. Notes on Jordan Form. Northwestern University, Department of Mathematics.
la-09-c2.quote: Any operator T on V can be represented by a matrix in Jordan form. This matrix is unique up to a rearrangement of the order of the Jordan blocks, and is called the Jordan form of T .
la-09-c2.claim: The Jordan form is unique up to the ordering of blocks, making it a complete invariant for similarity of matrices.

la-10-c1.text: Keith Conrad. Tensor Products. University of Connecticut, Department of Mathematics (expository notes).
la-10-c1.quote: Tensors in M ⊗R N that have the form m ⊗ n are called elementary tensors. (Other names for elementary tensors are simple tensors, decomposable tensors, pure tensors, and monomial tensors.)
la-10-c1.claim: The element u tensor v represents the "pure tensor" of u and v.

la-10-c2.text: Keith Conrad. Tensor Products. University of Connecticut, Department of Mathematics (expository notes).
la-10-c2.quote: The tensor product is the first concept in algebra whose properties make consistent sense only by a universal mapping property, which is: M ⊗R N is the universal object that turns bilinear maps on M × N into linear maps.
la-10-c2.claim: The tensor product is characterized by a universal property: every bilinear map V x W to Z factors uniquely through V tensor W.

la-11-c2.text: Steven G. Johnson (2019). Week 4: Lectures 9 and 10. MIT OpenCourseWare, 18.335J Introduction to Numerical Methods.
la-11-c2.quote: Gave the simple, but unstable, construction of the Gram-Schmidt algorithm, to find a QR factorization.
la-11-c2.claim: The classical Gram-Schmidt process is mathematically elegant but numerically unstable: rounding errors accumulate and the resulting vectors lose orthogonality.

la-11-c3.text: Jonathan Richard Shewchuk (1994). An Introduction to the Conjugate Gradient Method Without the Agonizing Pain. Carnegie Mellon University, School of Computer Science.
la-11-c3.quote: Factoring may be impossible due to limited memory, and will be time-consuming as well; even the backsolving step may be slower than iterative solution. On the other hand, most iterative methods are memory-efficient and run quickly with sparse matrices.
la-11-c3.claim: For large sparse systems (millions of unknowns), direct methods like Gaussian elimination are too expensive.

la-12-c1.text: (2003). COS 496 Computer Vision, Spring 2003: Eigenfaces assignment. Princeton University, Department of Computer Science.
la-12-c1.quote: Determine the top k principal components, corresponding to the eigenfaces with maximal variation.
la-12-c1.claim: Treating each face image as a high-dimensional vector, PCA finds the "directions" in face-space that capture the most variation.

la-12-c3.text: Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar, Jakob Uszkoreit, Llion Jones, Aidan N. Gomez, Lukasz Kaiser, Illia Polosukhin (2017). Attention Is All You Need. arXiv.
la-12-c3.quote: Multi-Head Attention consists of several attention layers running in parallel.
la-12-c3.claim: Multi-head attention runs several attention operations in parallel (each with different linear projections), then concatenates and linearly projects the results.
